sources.entry: Beszel | Lightweight server monitoring with Docker stats, history and alerts

summary.one_liner: Beszel is a lightweight server monitoring platform with a web dashboard, Docker/Podman container stats, historical data, and configurable alerts.
summary.what_it_does: Beszel has two components: a hub, a web app built on PocketBase that provides the dashboard, and an agent that runs on each monitored system and sends metrics to the hub. It tracks host CPU, memory (including swap and ZFS ARC), disk usage and I/O, network, load average, temperatures, fan speed, battery, and GPU usage/power for Nvidia, AMD, and Intel. It also reports status and CPU, memory, and network history for Docker/Podman containers, plus S.M.A.R.T. disk health and ZFS pool and dataset metrics. The README says it can monitor response time and interruptions from agents, send alerts for most metrics to many notification services, and perform automatic backups to disk or S3-compatible storage. It supports multiple users, OAuth/OIDC login (with password auth optionally disabled), and API access.
use_cases: monitor home server or VPS resources
track Docker container CPU and memory history
get alerts when a server or disk fails
share server dashboards across team members
how_to_run: Quick start instructions are on the project website, beszel.dev (not included in the README).
stack: Go (agent and hub, not named in README)
notable: Hub-and-agent architecture with a PocketBase-based web dashboard
Automatic backups to disk or S3-compatible storage
caveats: Setup details are only on the external website, not in the README
Support is community-driven; the maintainer may not always have time to respond
Some metrics (fan speed, mdraid) are Linux-specific based on the README
